query: FeNiCrCoCu is considered suitable for thin-film use, and its expense favors applying it as a protective coating on conventional metals rather than using it in bulk. Earlier studies examined room-temperature wear behavior in relation to coating–substrate combinations, composition, and grain size, but largely addressed the alloy itself or a limited thermal regime rather than the overall wear response of a coating across different temperatures. Under the constraints that FeNiCrCoCu remains a thin protective coating and that high-temperature wear is the target application, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs its overall wear resistance and why? Specify an intervention relative to a baseline coating condition, predict the observations expected if the hypothesis is correct, state the applicable temperature and loading boundaries, connect the hypothesis to prior evidence, and identify a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: At high service temperatures (400–700 °C) the overall wear resistance of thin-film FeNiCrCoCu coatings is governed primarily by the in-situ formation and retention of a dense, self-lubricating mixed-oxide glaze rich in Cr2O3 and CuO/CuCr2O4 spinel; promoting the growth of this oxide scale before sliding will lower the steady-state wear rate by at least 50 % relative to an un-oxidised coating because the glaze reduces metal/metal contact and provides solid-lubricant shear planes.
generation.material_initial_state: Magnetron-sputtered ~5 µm FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy coating on AISI 304 stainless steel, nanocrystalline (~20 nm) and in the as-deposited, metallic state (no deliberate heat treatment).
generation.intervention: Apply a controlled pre-oxidation heat treatment in air at 550 °C for 1 h to form a continuous Cr–Cu-rich oxide layer (~100 nm) on the coating surface before wear testing.
generation.conditions: Pin-on-disk wear tests in air at 500 °C, normal load 5 N, sliding speed 0.1 m s⁻¹, 1000 m sliding distance.
generation.structural_mediator: Continuous adherent Cr2O3 + CuO/CuCr2O4 composite glaze (≈100 nm) on and within the top 200 nm of the coating.
generation.mechanism: During high-temperature sliding the oxide glaze acts as a solid lubricant with low shear strength and high hardness, blocking direct asperity contact and trapping debris; Cu promotes plasticity and spinel formation, while Cr2O3 supplies hardness and thermodynamic stability. This combination lowers friction, limits abrasiveness, and protects the underlying metallic coating from oxidative and mechanical removal.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the baseline, the pre-oxidised coating will exhibit: 1) ≥50 % reduction in volumetric wear rate (mm³ N⁻¹ m⁻¹); 2) Coefficient of friction drop from ~0.7 to ≤0.4 after the running-in period; 3) Post-test XPS/TEM confirming retention of a continuous Cr–Cu spinel/oxide layer with only minor breakthrough to metallic substrate. No significant difference is expected at room temperature because the glaze is not stable there.
generation.baseline: Same coating tested in the as-deposited metallic state under identical sliding conditions.
generation.boundary: Temperature 400–700 °C; normal loads ≤7 N (contact pressures below oxide spallation threshold); sliding in oxidising environments (air). Below 300 °C or in inert gas the mechanism should not dominate.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of wear-rate reduction is extrapolated from analogous oxide-glaze behaviour in other Cr- and Cu-containing alloys; direct data for FeNiCrCoCu are presently lacking. It is uncertain whether the thin film’s residual stresses will impede oxide adhesion during sliding.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of identically sputtered FeNiCrCoCu coatings: (A) baseline metallic, (B) pre-oxidised at 550 °C/1 h. Conduct pin-on-disk wear tests in air at 500 °C under the stated load and speed for 1000 m. Characterise wear tracks by 3D profilometry (volume loss), measure friction in-situ, and analyse surfaces by XPS and cross-sectional TEM to confirm oxide structure.
measurements: Coefficient of friction vs. sliding distance
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the pre-oxidised coating (B) shows ≤10 % difference in wear rate relative to (A) OR lacks a continuous Cr–Cu oxide glaze after testing, the hypothesis is falsified.
